name: Solara Hibiscus-Mango
description: The undisputed king of Meridian 88's soda market, Solara Hibiscus-Mango is a lightly carbonated, synth-hibiscus and real-mango-extract blend with a signature deep crimson color. It is sold on every tier, in every vending corridor, in every transit hub — the drink that everyone from the Shelf to the Spire has at least tried.
flavor_profile: Tart-sweet hibiscus up front, a wave of ripe mango mid-palate, faintly floral finish with a clean effervescence; not too sweet, not too sharp
slogan: Every city. Every tier. One color.
cultural_context: Solara Hibiscus-Mango is so ubiquitous it functions as a social equalizer — a Shelf kid and a Spire exec have both tasted it. It appears in M88 idiom: 'basic as a red Solara' means something is universally understood. Street vendors sell counterfeit versions in hand-filled cans; Spire clubs serve it as a mixer. The can's deep red is instantly recognizable across all visual languages.
story_hooks: A street chemist has cracked Solara's proprietary synth-hibiscus compound and is undercutting the corponation's supply chain — Solara's enforcement division wants the formula back quietly, or the chemist erased.
A Shelf community running on recycled water has been diluting Solara cans to stretch supply; someone notices the diluted version tastes better and wants to know why.

A Tier 5 sommelier has published a tasting guide rating every regional Solara variant — and one variant, produced in a single Milwaukee sub-plant, has a contamination that produces a mild BCI-syncing euphoria.
